You are working in a Go repository checked out at /echo (this is the labstack/echo v4 web framework). There is a reported bug in /echo/middleware/proxy.go: when a proxy balancer has NO targets, calling Next() panics (randomBalancer: rand.Intn(0) panics; roundRobinBalancer: b.i % uint32(0) panics with integer divide by zero). The expected behavior (per the hidden test `middleware::TestProxyBalancerWithNoTargets`) is that this must not panic: Next() should return nil when there are no targets, and the Proxy middleware should then return an HTTP error (echo.ErrServiceUnavailable, i.e. 503) instead of panicking, without calling c.Set(config.ContextKey, ...) with a nil target.

Your job:
1. FIRST, before any edit, run the baseline test suite and record which tests fail: `cd /echo && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -50` (also `go build ./...`). Save the baseline failing test names.
2. Then implement the minimal fix in /echo/middleware/proxy.go:
   - In `func (b *randomBalancer) Next(c echo.Context) *ProxyTarget`, after acquiring the read lock, return nil if len(b.targets) == 0.
   - In `func (b *roundRobinBalancer) Next(c echo.Context) *ProxyTarget`, return nil if len(b.targets) == 0 (before the modulo).
   - In `ProxyWithConfig`'s returned handler, right after `tgt := config.Balancer.Next(c)`, add: `if tgt == nil { return echo.ErrServiceUnavailable }` (before `c.Set(config.ContextKey, tgt)`).
   Keep the change minimal and idiomatic; do not reformat unrelated code, do not touch any *_test.go file, do not change any other behavior.
3. Verify: `cd /echo && gofmt -l middleware/proxy.go` (must print nothing), `go vet ./middleware/`, `go build ./...`, and `go test ./middleware/... ./... 2>&1 | tail -40`. Confirm no NEW failures compared to the baseline (in particular TestProxy, TestProxyRealIPHeader, TestProxyRewrite, TestProxyRewriteRegex, TestProxy_1_11 must still pass).
4. Also write a temporary throwaway test in /tmp (NOT in the repository) or a small program that constructs a round-robin balancer and a random balancer with zero targets, wraps it with middleware.Proxy, serves a request through httptest, and confirms the response code is 503 and no panic occurs. Delete any temporary file you created inside /echo afterwards (verify with `git status --porcelain` that only middleware/proxy.go is modified).

Report back: the baseline failing tests, the exact diff you applied (git diff), the test results before/after, and confirmation that `git status --porcelain` shows only middleware/proxy.go modified.

You are working in a Go repository checked out at /echo (the labstack/echo v4 web framework). A reported bug is in /echo/context.go, in `func (c *context) Scheme() string` (search for `func (c *context) Scheme`). Expected behaviour, per the hidden tests `TestContext_Scheme`, `TestContext_Scheme/ignores_invalid_X-Forwarded-Proto_and_uses_X-Forwarded-Protocol` and `TestContext_Scheme/ignores_invalid_forwarded_headers_and_falls_back_to_http` (these tests are NOT in the repository; their names describe the expected behaviour):
- Scheme() must look at the `X-Forwarded-Proto` header first; if its value is NOT a valid scheme (valid values are exactly "http" and "https"), it must IGNORE that header and fall back to the next source (`X-Forwarded-Protocol`), and if that is also invalid, fall back to the TLS/URL scheme ("http" for a plain request).
- The current implementation likely returns the raw header value without validating it (e.g. it returns "invalid" or "ws" or similar when X-Forwarded-Proto is garbage), which is the bug.

Your job:
1. FIRST record the baseline: `cd /echo && go build ./... && go test -count=1 ./... 2>&1 | tail -30` (note any pre-existing failures; there should be none).
2. Read /echo/context.go around `Scheme()` and any related helper (e.g. `c.Echo().IPExtractor`, `c.request.Header.Get(echo.HeaderXForwardedProto)`, `HeaderXForwardedProtocol`, `HeaderXForwardedSsl`, `c.IsTLS()`, `c.request.URL.Scheme`). Also read the existing tests in /echo/context_test.go for Scheme to understand the current expectations (do NOT modify them). Determine the minimal fix so that invalid values of X-Forwarded-Proto (and invalid X-Forwarded-Protocol) are ignored and the code falls back to http/https correctly.
3. Implement the minimal, idiomatic fix in /echo/context.go only. Do NOT modify any *_test.go file. Do NOT reformat unrelated code. Do NOT add new features.
4. Verify: `gofmt -l context.go` (must print nothing), `go vet ./...`, `go build ./...`, `go test -count=1 ./... 2>&1 | tail -30` — no NEW failures versus baseline (in particular all existing context tests and TestContext_Scheme must pass).
5. Also write a throwaway program/test OUTSIDE the repository (e.g. /tmp/schemecheck, external module with `replace github.com/labstack/echo/v4 => /echo`, run with GOPROXY=off) that serves requests with headers: X-Forwarded-Proto: https -> expect https; X-Forwarded-Proto: invalid -> expect http; X-Forwarded-Proto: invalid + X-Forwarded-Protocol: https -> expect https; no headers -> expect http. Delete the throwaway files afterwards.
6. Confirm with `cd /echo && git status --porcelain` that the only files modified are context.go, router.go and middleware/proxy.go (the latter two were fixed by other agents — leave them alone).

Report back: the exact defect (file:line), the diff (`git diff context.go`), baseline vs post-fix test results, the results of your header checks, and `git status --porcelain`.

You are working in a Go repository checked out at /echo (the labstack/echo v4 web framework). A reported bug is in /echo/group.go. Expected behaviour, per the hidden test `TestMultipleGroupSamePathMiddleware` (NOT in the repository; its name describes expected behaviour): when two different groups register the SAME route path (e.g. `g1 := e.Group("/api", mw1)`, `g2 := e.Group("/api", mw2)` or two groups with the same prefix), each registered route must keep the middleware of the group it was registered on — i.e. a request to a route added via g1 must run g1's middleware and a route added via g2 must run g2's middleware. The current code likely shares/overwrites the middleware slice between groups (e.g. `Group`/`Add` appending to a slice whose backing array is shared, so adding middleware to one group silently mutates another group's routes, or the route's middleware slice is aliased).

Your job:
1. FIRST record the baseline: `cd /echo && go build ./... && go test -count=1 ./... 2>&1 | tail -30` (note pre-existing failures; there should be none).
2. Read /echo/group.go fully (especially `Group`, `Add`, `Use`, `Any`, `Match`, `Static`, `File`) and /echo/echo.go's `Add`/`add` route registration to see how middleware slices are stored and aliased. Also read /echo/group_test.go (do NOT modify any test file) to understand the intended semantics. Determine the concrete defect and the minimal fix (most likely: copy the middleware slice when creating a group / when registering a route, so later `Use`/`Group` calls cannot mutate already-registered routes).
3. Implement the minimal, idiomatic fix in /echo/group.go (and only there, unless the fix genuinely must live in echo.go — in that case keep it minimal and explain). Do NOT modify any *_test.go file. Do NOT reformat unrelated code. Do NOT add new features.
4. Verify: `gofmt -l group.go` (must print nothing), `go vet ./...`, `go build ./...`, `go test -count=1 ./... 2>&1 | tail -30` — no NEW failures versus baseline.
5. Also write a throwaway program/test OUTSIDE the repository (e.g. /tmp/groupcheck, external module with `replace github.com/labstack/echo/v4 => /echo`, run with GOPROXY=off) that builds an echo instance with two groups on the same path, each with a distinct middleware that sets a header or records a value, registers a route on each group, and asserts each request only runs its own group's middleware (also test a group created with `e.Group("/x", mw)` followed by `g.Use(mw2)` after routes were registered). Delete the throwaway files afterwards.
6. Confirm with `cd /echo && git status --porcelain` that the only modified files are group.go plus bind.go, context.go, router.go, middleware/proxy.go (fixed by other agents — leave them alone).

Report back: the exact defect (file:line), the diff (`git diff group.go`), baseline vs post-fix test results, the results of your multi-group checks, and `git status --porcelain`.

You are working in a Go repository checked out at /echo (the labstack/echo v4 web framework). A reported bug is in /echo/bind.go, in the default binder's handling of binding data into a `map`. Expected behaviour, per the hidden tests `TestDefaultBinder_bindDataToMap` and `TestDefaultBinder_bindDataToMap/ok,_bind_to_map[string][]string` (NOT in the repository; the names describe expected behaviour): when the bind target is a map (e.g. `map[string]interface{}`, `map[string]string`, or `map[string][]string`), `bindData` must populate it correctly from the request data (query params / form values / JSON body), including the case of binding to `map[string][]string` where repeated values must all be collected.

Your job:
1. FIRST record the baseline: `cd /echo && go build ./... && go test -count=1 ./... 2>&1 | tail -30` (note pre-existing failures; there should be none).
2. Read /echo/bind.go carefully, especially `func (b *DefaultBinder) bindData(destination interface{}, data map[string][]string, tag string) error` and its map handling branch, plus `bindDataToMap` if present, and the existing tests in /echo/bind_test.go and /echo/binder_test.go (do NOT modify any test file). Determine the concrete defect: e.g. for `map[string][]string` the code may assign only the first value (`v[0]`), or it may fail/panic on a nil map, or it may not handle the value type correctly. Reason from the code and doc comments only.
3. Implement the minimal, idiomatic fix in /echo/bind.go only. Do NOT modify any *_test.go file. Do NOT reformat unrelated code. Do NOT add new features.
4. Verify: `gofmt -l bind.go` (must print nothing), `go vet ./...`, `go build ./...`, `go test -count=1 ./... 2>&1 | tail -30` — no NEW failures versus baseline.
5. Also write a throwaway program/test OUTSIDE the repository (e.g. /tmp/bindcheck, external module with `replace github.com/labstack/echo/v4 => /echo`, run with GOPROXY=off) that binds query/form data with repeated keys into `map[string][]string`, `map[string]string` and `map[string]interface{}` and asserts the resulting values. Delete the throwaway files afterwards.
6. Confirm with `cd /echo && git status --porcelain` that the only modified files are bind.go plus context.go, router.go, middleware/proxy.go (fixed by other agents — leave them alone).

Report back: the exact defect (file:line), the diff (`git diff bind.go`), baseline vs post-fix test results, the results of your map-binding checks, and `git status --porcelain`.

You are working in a Go repository checked out at /echo (the labstack/echo v4 web framework). A reported bug is in /echo/middleware/compress.go. Expected behaviour, per the hidden test `middleware::TestGzipEmpty` (NOT in the repository; its name describes expected behaviour): when the response body is EMPTY (a handler that writes nothing, e.g. just returns 200 with no body), the Gzip compression middleware must NOT write a gzip-compressed (non-empty) body — the response must stay empty (no gzip magic bytes / no compressed payload). The current code likely always writes a gzip stream (or writes the gzip header) even when nothing was written, producing a non-empty body (or an invalid/empty gzip stream) for an empty response.

Your job:
1. FIRST record the baseline: `cd /echo && go build ./... && go test -count=1 ./... 2>&1 | tail -30` (note pre-existing failures; there should be none).
2. Read /echo/middleware/compress.go fully (the `gzipResponseWriter`, its `Write`, `Close`, `Flush`, `Hijack`, `Header`, `WriteHeader` methods, and the middleware func) and /echo/middleware/compress_test.go (do NOT modify any test file). Determine the concrete defect and the minimal fix so that an empty response body produces an empty response body (e.g. do not write the gzip header/stream when nothing was written, or skip compression when the body is empty; keep the Content-Encoding behaviour consistent with the existing tests, which must keep passing).
3. Implement the minimal, idiomatic fix in /echo/middleware/compress.go only. Do NOT modify any *_test.go file. Do NOT reformat unrelated code. Do NOT add new features.
4. Verify: `gofmt -l middleware/compress.go` (must print nothing), `go vet ./...`, `go build ./...`, `go test -count=1 ./... 2>&1 | tail -30` — no NEW failures versus baseline (all existing compress tests must still pass).
5. Also write a throwaway program/test OUTSIDE the repository (e.g. /tmp/compresscheck, external module with `replace github.com/labstack/echo/v4 => /echo`, run with GOPROXY=off) that serves: (a) a handler writing nothing -> assert response body length is 0 and no gzip magic bytes, (b) a handler writing "hello" -> assert body decompresses to "hello", (c) a handler writing a large body -> assert it is gzipped and decompresses correctly. Delete the throwaway files afterwards.
6. Confirm with `cd /echo && git status --porcelain` that the only modified files are middleware/compress.go plus bind.go, context.go, group.go, router.go, middleware/proxy.go (fixed by other agents — leave them alone).

Report back: the exact defect (file:line), the diff (`git diff middleware/compress.go`), baseline vs post-fix test results, the results of your empty/compressed body checks, and `git status --porcelain`.

You are working in a Go repository checked out at /echo (the labstack/echo v4 web framework). A reported bug is in /echo/router.go: the expected behaviour is that when a request path is not routable (no route matches the path, e.g. the router's `Find` is called with a method/path for which no route was registered, or a path that cannot be routed), Echo must return an HTTP 404 Not Found error rather than panicking, hanging, or returning a wrong status. The hidden test that checks this is named `TestRouterNoRoutablePath` (it is NOT in the repository; its name describes the expected behaviour).

Your job:
1. FIRST record the baseline: `cd /echo && go build ./... && go test -count=1 ./... 2>&1 | tail -30`. Note which tests fail before your edit (there should be none).
2. Read /echo/router.go carefully (especially the `Find` method, the `Router`/`router` struct, `insert`, `add`, and any place that indexes into route slices or node children without checking bounds, and any place that can panic or return a nil handler). Identify the concrete defect that makes a non-routable path misbehave (e.g. index-out-of-range panic, nil pointer dereference, wrong error returned, infinite loop). Reason from the code and the doc comments in the repo; do not rely on outside knowledge of the upstream project.
3. Implement the minimal, idiomatic fix in /echo/router.go only. Do NOT change any *_test.go file. Do NOT reformat unrelated code. Do NOT implement new features.
4. Verify: `gofmt -l router.go` (must print nothing), `go vet ./...`, `go build ./...`, and `go test -count=1 ./... 2>&1 | tail -30` — no NEW failures versus baseline. Also write a throwaway program/test OUTSIDE the repository (e.g. in /tmp/routercheck, an external module with `replace github.com/labstack/echo/v4 => /echo`, run with GOFLAGS=-mod=mod GOPROXY=off) that creates an `echo.New()`, registers some routes, and serves requests for paths that match no route (including paths like "/", "//", "/a/b/c", paths with trailing slashes, and unusual methods) asserting the response status is 404 and that nothing panics. Delete the throwaway files afterwards.
5. Confirm with `cd /echo && git status --porcelain` that the only modified file is router.go (plus middleware/proxy.go which another agent already fixed — leave it alone).

Report back: the exact defect found (with file:line), the diff you applied (`git diff router.go`), the baseline vs post-fix test results, the results of your no-routable-path checks, and `git status --porcelain`.
